<h2>Diagnose sjSDM CV Preparation Endpoints</h2>

<h3>Description</h3>

<p>Diagnoses whether requested prepared-fold targets exist, have successful
metadata and content hashes, and can be read from a targets store.
</p>


<h3>Usage</h3>

<pre><code class='language-R'>diagnose_sjsdm_cv_preparation_endpoints(
  store_path = NULL,
  target_names = NULL,
  load_metadata_function = load_targets_store_metadata,
  read_target_function = targets::tar_read_raw
)
</code></pre>


<h3>Arguments</h3>

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td><code id="store_path">store_path</code></td>
<td>
<p>Character scalar identifying the targets store.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="target_names">target_names</code></td>
<td>
<p>Unique non-empty character vector of prepared-fold target names.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="load_metadata_function">load_metadata_function</code></td>
<td>
<p>Injectable target-metadata loader.</p>
</td></tr>
<tr><td><code id="read_target_function">read_target_function</code></td>
<td>
<p>Injectable raw target reader.</p>
</td></tr>
</table>


<h3>Details</h3>

<p>Endpoint statuses are 'prepared', 'missing', 'errored', 'unreadable', or
'cache_format_incompatible'. The last status is reserved for legacy 'qs'
objects that current 'qs2'-based targets installations cannot read.
</p>


<h3>Value</h3>

<p>A tibble with one row per requested target and its endpoint status, data
hash, and diagnostic message.
</p>

</main>
